headline: Git Brain brings JetBrains-style Git GUI to VS Code, Cursor
summary: New VS Code extension offers a visual commit graph, AI Git workflows, and a 3-way merge editor, aiming to streamline developer workflows.
details: Git Brain is a new visual Git GUI designed to bring a JetBrains-style experience to VS Code, Cursor, and other VS Code-compatible IDEs. It aims to provide a more intuitive and integrated Git workflow for developers, serving as an alternative to tools like GitLens.

The extension features a visual commit graph that displays branches, merges, and tags, allowing developers to easily inspect commit details and file diffs without leaving the graph. This visual approach aims to make it easier to reconstruct repository states compared to traditional command-line interfaces.

Git Brain also includes a robust 3-way merge editor to simplify conflict resolution. It allows users to view and edit conflicting versions side-by-side, making complex merge scenarios more manageable.

A key aspect of Git Brain is its integration with AI coding agents. Tools like Claude, Codex, and Copilot can leverage Git Brain to analyze changes, split them into logical commits, generate commit messages, summarize changes, and assist with PR descriptions and conflict resolution.

The extension provides structured Git context to agents, moving beyond simple file access and shell commands. This allows agents to interact with Git capabilities with defined guardrails, which is crucial as AI gains more autonomy in development tasks.

Git Brain also enhances the usability of Git worktrees, offering a dedicated visual panel for creating, inspecting, opening, and removing them. This feature is particularly useful for developers managing multiple parallel tasks or agents.
With over 70,000 downloads on Open VSX, Git Brain has quickly gained traction since its inception, driven by a desire to improve the everyday Git workflow for both human developers and AI agents.

The project's goal is to create a unified Git experience where humans benefit from a clear visual interface and AI agents receive structured Git capabilities, all operating on the same repository state.
